chapter_text:
CHAPTER 11 — रचनाकौशलम् (RACHANAKAUSHALAM)

Introduction — रचनाकौशलम् किम्?

रचना (rachana) means "composition" or "creating something out of words", and कौशलम् (kaushalam) means "skill". So रचनाकौशलम् is the SKILL OF COMPOSING in Sanskrit — the practical ability to build correct, meaningful Sanskrit yourself, rather than only reading verses that others have written. In earlier lessons you learnt to READ Sanskrit; in this lesson you learn to WRITE it. A student who can form a correct sentence (वाक्यरचना), write a letter (पत्रलेखनम्), compose a paragraph or short essay (अनुच्छेदः / निबन्धः), translate between Hindi/English and Sanskrit (अनुवादः), and describe a picture (चित्रवर्णनम्) has truly made the language his own. This chapter teaches each of these five composition skills with worked Sanskrit examples and model answers, and ends with the grammar and usage (कारक-विभक्ति, सन्धि, समास) that every good composition needs.

Why composition matters (रचनायाः महत्त्वम्)

Reading tells you what a language SAYS; composition proves that you can MAKE the language say what YOU mean. When you compose, you must choose the right word (शब्दः), give it the right ending (विभक्तिः / रूपम्), make the verb agree with the subject (कर्तृ-क्रिया-सामञ्जस्यम्), and arrange the words in a natural order. Every mistake shows up at once, so composition is the fastest way to master grammar. It also builds confidence: once you can write "अहं प्रतिदिनं संस्कृतं पठामि" ("I read Sanskrit every day") without help, the language stops being a puzzle and becomes a tool.

Section 1 — वाक्यरचना (Sentence formation)

A Sanskrit sentence (वाक्यम्) at its simplest has three parts: the doer कर्ता (subject), the thing done-to कर्म (object), and the action क्रिया (verb). The natural order is कर्ता — कर्म — क्रिया (Subject — Object — Verb), for example: बालकः फलं खादति ("The boy eats a fruit"). Here बालकः is the कर्ता in प्रथमा विभक्ति (nominative), फलम् is the कर्म in द्वितीया विभक्ति (accusative), and खादति is the क्रिया.

The single most important rule of वाक्यरचना is कर्तृ-क्रिया agreement: the VERB must agree with the SUBJECT in NUMBER (वचन) and PERSON (पुरुषः). Sanskrit has three numbers — एकवचन (one), द्विवचन (two) and बहुवचन (many). Watch the verb change with the subject:
  • बालकः पठति। — One boy reads. (एकवचन)
  • बालकौ पठतः। — Two boys read. (द्विवचन)
  • बालकाः पठन्ति। — (Many) boys read. (बहुवचन)
The subject-ending and the verb-ending change TOGETHER; बालकाः पठति (plural subject, singular verb) is WRONG.

Sanskrit also changes the verb by PERSON. Using the root पठ् (to read) in the present tense (लट् लकार):
  • प्रथम पुरुष (he/she/they): सः पठति, तौ पठतः, ते पठन्ति.
  • मध्यम पुरुष (you): त्वं पठसि, युवां पठथः, यूयं पठथ.
  • उत्तम पुरुष (I/we): अहं पठामि, आवां पठावः, वयं पठामः.
So "I read" is अहं पठामि, "you read" is त्वं पठसि, "they read" is ते पठन्ति. To make a sentence NEGATIVE, put न before the verb: सः न पठति ("he does not read"). To make a QUESTION, use a question-word such as किम् (what / yes-no), कुत्र (where), कदा (when): सः कुत्र गच्छति? ("Where does he go?").

Section 2 — पत्रलेखनम् (Letter writing)

A letter (पत्रम्) may be औपचारिकम् (formal) or अनौपचारिकम् (informal). A FORMAL letter — such as a प्रार्थनापत्रम् (application) to the principal — follows a fixed skeleton: (1) सेवायाम् ("To…") with the addressee and address; (2) दिनाङ्कः (date); (3) विषयः (the subject line, one line saying what the letter is about); (4) सम्बोधनम् (salutation) such as महोदय / मान्यवर ("Respected Sir"); (5) the body (विषय-वस्तु); (6) the closing भवदीयः (male) or भवदीया (female), with the writer's name (प्रेषकः / नाम).

Model formal letter (आदर्श-औपचारिक-पत्रम्) — a two-day leave application:

सेवायाम्,
श्रीमान् प्रधानाचार्यः,
शासकीय-उच्च-विद्यालयः, अमुकनगरम्।
दिनाङ्कः — १० जुलै, २०२६
विषयः — द्विदिनावकाशार्थं प्रार्थनापत्रम्।
महोदय,
सविनयं निवेदनम् अस्ति यत् अहं ज्वरेण पीडितः अस्मि, अतः विद्यालयम् आगन्तुं न शक्नोमि। कृपया मह्यं द्वयोः दिनयोः (१०-११ जुलै) अवकाशं दातुम् अर्हन्ति। अहं भवतां कृते सदा कृतज्ञः भविष्यामि।
सधन्यवादम्।
भवदीयः शिष्यः,
रमेशः, दशमी कक्षा।

An INFORMAL letter (to a friend or family member) is warmer and shorter. It opens with प्रियमित्र / प्रिय सखे ("Dear friend") or पूज्ये मातः ("Respected Mother"), uses सप्रेम नमः / सादरं प्रणामाः as greeting, and closes with भवतः मित्रम् / तव सुहृद् ("your friend"). Example opening and closing:
  प्रिय सखे मोहन, सप्रेम नमः। … (body) … त्वं मम जन्मदिवसे अवश्यम् आगच्छ। भवतः मित्रम्, सुरेशः।

Section 3 — अनुच्छेदलेखनम् (Paragraph / essay writing)

An अनुच्छेदः (paragraph) is a small group of connected sentences (usually five to eight) all about ONE topic; a longer, several-paragraph composition is a निबन्धः (essay). A good paragraph has three parts: (1) आरम्भः — an opening/topic sentence that names the subject; (2) विस्तारः — the middle, giving details; (3) उपसंहारः — a concluding sentence that rounds off the idea. Stay on ONE topic and keep the sentences simple and connected.

Model paragraph (आदर्श-अनुच्छेदः) — "मम विद्यालयः" (My school):

मम विद्यालयः अतीव सुन्दरः अस्ति। सः नगरस्य मध्ये स्थितः अस्ति। विद्यालये बहवः अध्यापकाः छात्राः च सन्ति। अत्र एकं पुस्तकालयः क्रीडाङ्गणं च अस्ति। अध्यापकाः अस्मान् सम्यक् पाठयन्ति। अहं मम विद्यालयं बहु स्निह्यामि।

(Translation: My school is very beautiful. It is situated in the middle of the town. In the school there are many teachers and students. Here there is a library and a playground. The teachers teach us well. I love my school very much.) Notice how the first sentence names the topic, the middle sentences add details, and the last sentence concludes with a feeling.

Section 4 — अनुवादः (Translation)

Translation (अनुवादः) means carrying a sentence from one language into another WITHOUT losing its meaning. To translate Hindi/English INTO Sanskrit, ask three questions: Who is the doer (→ प्रथमा, कर्ता)? What is acted upon (→ द्वितीया, कर्म)? What is the action, and does its ending match the subject's number/person? Worked examples:
  • Hindi: मैं विद्यालय जाता हूँ। → Sanskrit: अहं विद्यालयं गच्छामि। (I go to school.)
  • Hindi: वह पुस्तक पढ़ती है। → सा पुस्तकं पठति। (She reads a book.)
  • Hindi: सूरज उगता है। → सूर्यः उदयति। (The sun rises.)
  • English: The boys play. → बालकाः क्रीडन्ति।
  • English: We are students. → वयं छात्राः स्मः।
  • English: I have a book. → मम पुस्तकम् अस्ति। (lit. "of me there is a book" — Sanskrit uses षष्ठी + अस्ति for "have").
The commonest mistakes are (a) forgetting the द्वितीया ending on the object (writing विद्यालयः गच्छामि instead of विद्यालयं गच्छामि) and (b) a verb that does not agree with the subject. Translate the MEANING, not word-for-word.

Section 5 — चित्रवर्णनम् (Picture description)

चित्रवर्णनम् means describing a picture (चित्रम्) in words. It is normally written in the PRESENT tense (लट् लकार), in about five simple sentences, naming the things (वस्तूनि) in the scene, their colours (वर्णाः) and the actions (क्रियाः) happening. A very useful frame is चित्रे … अस्ति / सन्ति ("in the picture there is / there are"); note that चित्रे is सप्तमी विभक्ति (locative, "in the picture").

Model picture description (उद्यान-चित्रम्, a garden):
  चित्रे एकम् उद्यानम् अस्ति। उद्याने बहवः वृक्षाः पुष्पाणि च सन्ति। आकाशे खगाः उड्डयन्ते। बालकाः उद्याने क्रीडन्ति। दृश्यम् अतीव रमणीयम् अस्ति।
(In the picture there is a garden. In the garden there are many trees and flowers. Birds fly in the sky. Children play in the garden. The scene is very lovely.)

Section 6 — व्याकरण-प्रयोगः (Grammar and usage for composition)

Good composition rests on three grammar skills.

(A) कारक and विभक्ति. The कारक is the ROLE a noun plays towards the verb; the विभक्ति is the ENDING that shows it. The main pairs are:
  • कर्ता (doer) → प्रथमा: रामः गच्छति ("Rama goes").
  • कर्म (object) → द्वितीया: रामः फलं खादति ("Rama eats a fruit").
  • करण (instrument, "by/with") → तृतीया: सः हस्तेन लिखति ("he writes with the hand").
  • सम्प्रदान (recipient, "to/for") → चतुर्थी: सः गुरवे नमति ("he bows to the teacher").
  • अपादान (source, "from") → पञ्चमी: वृक्षात् पत्रं पतति ("a leaf falls from the tree").
  • सम्बन्ध (relation, "of") → षष्ठी: रामस्य पुस्तकम् ("Rama's book").
  • अधिकरण (location, "in/on/at") → सप्तमी: सः ग्रामे वसति ("he lives in the village").
Choosing the right विभक्ति is the heart of correct writing.

(B) सन्धि (euphonic joining). When words meet, sounds merge; you must both JOIN correctly and be able to SPLIT (सन्धि-विच्छेदः). Common examples used in composition:
  • देव + आलयः = देवालयः (अ + आ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
  • सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः (अ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धि).
  • विद्या + आलयः = विद्यालयः (आ + आ = आ).
  • न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ + अ = आ).
  • सत् + जनः = सज्जनः (व्यञ्जन-सन्धि).

(C) समास (compounding). Two or more words combine into one compact word — very useful for tight writing:
  • रामलक्ष्मणौ = राम च लक्ष्मणः च — द्वन्द्व-समासः.
  • राजपुत्रः = राज्ञः पुत्रः — तत्पुरुष-समासः.
  • नीलकमलम् = नीलं कमलम् — कर्मधारय-समासः.
  • पीताम्बरः = पीतम् अम्बरं यस्य सः — बहुव्रीहि-समासः.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you learned रचनाकौशलम् — the practical skill of composing in Sanskrit. You practised वाक्यरचना (building कर्ता-कर्म-क्रिया sentences with correct कर्तृ-क्रिया agreement and person/number), पत्रलेखनम् (formal प्रार्थनापत्र with सेवायाम्/विषयः/महोदय/भवदीयः, and warm informal letters), अनुच्छेदलेखनम् (a three-part paragraph — आरम्भः, विस्तारः, उपसंहारः — with a model on मम विद्यालयः), अनुवादः (translating Hindi/English into Sanskrit by fixing कर्ता, कर्म and verb-agreement), and चित्रवर्णनम् (five present-tense sentences using चित्रे … अस्ति/सन्ति). Finally you revised the grammar every composition needs: the six कारक with their विभक्ति, common सन्धि (देवालयः, सूर्योदयः, नास्ति, सज्जनः) with सन्धि-विच्छेद, and the four समास (द्वन्द्व, तत्पुरुष, कर्मधारय, बहुव्रीहि). Practise writing a little Sanskrit every day — that is the surest path to fluency.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the structure of a simple Sanskrit sentence (कर्ता-कर्म-क्रिया) and the rule of कर्तृ-क्रिया agreement in number and person.
Form correct Sanskrit sentences in singular, dual and plural, including negatives and questions, and correct agreement errors.
Recall the parts and conventions of formal and informal Sanskrit letters — सेवायाम्, विषयः, महोदय, भवदीयः/भवदीया, प्रिय सखे, भवतः मित्रम्.
Write a well-structured formal प्रार्थनापत्र and an informal letter in Sanskrit for a given situation.
Compose a coherent अनुच्छेद/निबन्ध on a given topic with a clear beginning, middle and conclusion.
Translate simple sentences between Hindi/English and Sanskrit, keeping correct case-endings and subject–verb agreement.
Describe a given picture in several present-tense Sanskrit sentences, naming objects, colours and actions.

chapter_summary.title: रचनाकौशलम् (Rachanakaushalam) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Secondary Sanskrit (209) summary for Chapter 11. It teaches the practical skill of composing in Sanskrit — forming sentences, writing letters, composing paragraphs and essays, translating, and describing pictures — with worked examples and the grammar every composition needs.

branches.label: वाक्यरचना — Sentences
details: न for negation, किम्/कुत्र for questions

sections.heading: Forming Sanskrit sentences (वाक्यरचना)
bullets: A simple sentence has कर्ता (subject, प्रथमा), कर्म (object, द्वितीया) and क्रिया (verb), usually in that order.
The verb must agree with the subject in number and person: बालकः पठति / बालकौ पठतः / बालकाः पठन्ति.
Add न before the verb for negatives (सः न पठति) and use किम्/कुत्र/कदा for questions.

sections.heading: Writing letters (पत्रलेखनम्)
bullets: A formal letter follows सेवायाम् → विषयः → महोदय → body → भवदीयः/भवदीया with the sender's name.
A प्रार्थनापत्र (application) states its purpose in the विषयः line.
An informal letter is warm: प्रिय सखे … सप्रेम नमः … भवतः मित्रम्.

sections.heading: Paragraphs, essays and translation
bullets: An अनुच्छेद has three parts: आरम्भः (opening), विस्तारः (details), उपसंहारः (conclusion); a निबन्धः is a longer essay.
Keep to ONE topic with simple connected sentences.
Translate by fixing the कर्ता, the कर्म (द्वितीया) and subject–verb agreement — meaning first, not word-for-word.

sections.heading: Describing a picture (चित्रवर्णनम्)
bullets: Write about five present-tense sentences describing the scene.
Use the frame चित्रे … अस्ति / सन्ति ('in the picture there is / are'); चित्रे is सप्तमी.
Name the objects, their colours, and the actions happening.

sections.heading: Grammar for composition (कारक, सन्धि, समास)
bullets: Six कारक map to विभक्ति: कर्ता–प्रथमा, कर्म–द्वितीया, करण–तृतीया, सम्प्रदान–चतुर्थी, अपादान–पञ्चमी, अधिकरण–सप्तमी.
सन्धि merges sounds: देव+आलयः=देवालयः, सूर्य+उदयः=सूर्योदयः, न+अस्ति=नास्ति; splitting back is सन्धि-विच्छेद.
समास compacts words: द्वन्द्व (रामलक्ष्मणौ), तत्पुरुष (राजपुत्रः), कर्मधारय, बहुव्रीहि.

key_takeaways: रचनाकौशलम् is the skill of COMPOSING in Sanskrit — writing, not just reading.
Every sentence needs कर्ता–कर्म–क्रिया with the verb agreeing in number and person.
A formal letter uses सेवायाम्/विषयः/महोदय/भवदीयः; an informal one uses प्रिय सखे/भवतः मित्रम्.
A good paragraph has आरम्भः, विस्तारः and उपसंहारः, all on one topic.
Translate by fixing कर्ता, कर्म (द्वितीया) and verb-agreement — carry the meaning, not the words.
चित्रवर्णन is written in the present tense with the frame चित्रे … अस्ति/सन्ति.
Composition rests on कारक-विभक्ति, सन्धि (with सन्धि-विच्छेद) and समास.

glossary.definition: The skill of composing in Sanskrit — forming sentences, letters, paragraphs, translations and picture descriptions.
Sentence formation: building कर्ता–कर्म–क्रिया with correct endings and agreement.
The doer/subject of a sentence, put in प्रथमा विभक्ति (nominative).
The object of a sentence, put in द्वितीया विभक्ति (accusative).
The verb; it agrees with the subject in number (वचन) and person (पुरुष).
An application/request letter, e.g. a leave application to the principal.
The one-line subject of a formal letter stating its purpose.
A paragraph: connected sentences on one topic with आरम्भः, विस्तारः, उपसंहारः.
An essay — a longer, multi-paragraph composition.
Translation — carrying a sentence's meaning from one language into another.
Describing a picture in present-tense sentences using चित्रे … अस्ति/सन्ति.
The role a noun plays towards the verb; shown by its विभक्ति (case ending).
A compound joining words into one, e.g. द्वन्द्व, तत्पुरुष, कर्मधारय, बहुव्रीहि.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — रचनाकौशलम् (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 11)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit in Devanagari and give explanations in English where asked. Refer to the model letters and paragraphs in the lesson.

questions.question: The कर्ता (subject) of a Sanskrit sentence takes which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: The doer is in प्रथमा (nominative).

questions.question: Give the present-tense forms of पठ् for अहम्, त्वम् and सः.
questions.answer: अहम् → पठामि; त्वम् → पठसि; सः → पठति.
questions.explanation: Verb changes with पुरुष.

questions.question: A request/application letter is called ____ .
questions.explanation: प्रार्थनापत्रम् = application letter.

questions.question: Which salutation and closing are used in a formal letter to the principal?
questions.explanation: Formal conventions.

questions.question: चित्रवर्णन is written in the present tense.
questions.explanation: Picture description uses the present tense (लट्).

questions.question: Write a short informal letter in Sanskrit (5–6 lines) inviting a friend to your birthday.
questions.answer: प्रिय सखे मोहन, सप्रेम नमः। आगामिनि रविवासरे मम जन्मदिवसः अस्ति। मम गृहे लघु-उत्सवः भविष्यति। त्वं सायं पञ्चवादने अवश्यम् आगच्छ। तव आगमनेन अहं प्रसन्नः भविष्यामि। भवतः मित्रम्, सुरेशः।
questions.explanation: Warm informal letter with प्रिय सखे and भवतः मित्रम्.

questions.question: Write a short अनुच्छेद (5–6 sentences) in Sanskrit on 'मम विद्यालयः'.
questions.answer: मम विद्यालयः अतीव सुन्दरः अस्ति। सः नगरस्य मध्ये स्थितः अस्ति। विद्यालये बहवः अध्यापकाः छात्राः च सन्ति। अत्र पुस्तकालयः क्रीडाङ्गणं च अस्ति। अध्यापकाः अस्मान् सम्यक् पाठयन्ति। अहं मम विद्यालयं बहु स्निह्यामि।
questions.explanation: Three-part paragraph on one topic (आरम्भः–विस्तारः–उपसंहारः).

questions.question: Translate into Sanskrit: 'I drink water.' and 'The boys play.'
questions.explanation: Fix कर्ता, कर्म and agreeing verb.

questions.question: Read: 'रामः ग्रामे हस्तेन पत्रं लिखति।' State the कारक/विभक्ति of ग्रामे, हस्तेन and पत्रम्.
questions.answer: ग्रामे = अधिकरण/सप्तमी; हस्तेन = करण/तृतीया; पत्रम् = कर्म/द्वितीया.
questions.explanation: Each noun's role is shown by its ending.

questions.question: सन्धि: देव + आलयः = ____ .
questions.explanation: अ + आ = आ (दीर्घ-सन्धि).

questions.question: In a simple Sanskrit sentence, the doer (कर्ता) takes which विभक्ति (case)?
questions.explanation: The कर्ता (subject) is in प्रथमा विभक्ति (nominative).

questions.question: 'The boy reads' is correctly written as
questions.explanation: कर्ता बालकः (प्रथमा) + क्रिया पठति.

questions.question: In 'बालकः पठति', the verb agrees with the subject in
questions.explanation: कर्तृ-क्रिया agreement is by वचन (number) and पुरुष (person).

questions.question: The plural of 'बालकः पठति' (the boys read) is
questions.explanation: बहुवचन subject बालकाः + बहुवचन verb पठन्ति.

questions.question: The dual form (two boys read) is
questions.explanation: द्विवचन subject बालकौ + द्विवचन verb पठतः.

questions.question: In 'सः जलं पिबति', the कर्म (object) is
questions.explanation: जलम् is the object in द्वितीया विभक्ति.

questions.question: The most typical/natural word order in a Sanskrit sentence is
questions.explanation: The usual order is कर्ता — कर्म — क्रिया.

questions.question: 'अहं गच्छामि' means
questions.explanation: अहम् = I, गच्छामि = (I) go.

questions.question: The verb form for 'they go' (बहुवचन) is
questions.explanation: प्रथम पुरुष बहुवचन of गम् = गच्छन्ति.

questions.question: To make a sentence negative, which word is placed before the verb?
questions.explanation: न before the verb negates it: सः न पठति.

questions.question: Which is a correctly formed sentence?
questions.explanation: Subject in प्रथमा (छात्रः), object in द्वितीया (विद्यालयम्), agreeing verb.

questions.question: In 'त्वं पठसि', the verb पठसि is in which पुरुष (person)?
questions.explanation: पठसि is मध्यम पुरुष एकवचन ('you read').

questions.question: Change to plural: 'वृक्षः अस्ति' →
questions.explanation: बहुवचन subject वृक्षाः + बहुवचन verb सन्ति.

questions.question: 'She writes a letter' is
questions.explanation: सा (she) + पत्रम् (object, द्वितीया) + लिखति.

questions.question: The correct verb form for 'अहम्' with root पठ् is
questions.explanation: उत्तम पुरुष एकवचन = पठामि.

questions.question: 'The two girls sing' is
questions.explanation: द्विवचन subject बालिके + द्विवचन verb गायतः.

questions.question: Fill the कर्म: 'रामः ___ गच्छति' (to the forest).
questions.explanation: Goal of motion takes द्वितीया: वनम्.

questions.question: Which sentence uses तृतीया (by/with) correctly?
questions.explanation: Instrument (करण) takes तृतीया: हस्तेन.

questions.question: 'सः कुत्र गच्छति?' means
questions.explanation: कुत्र = where.

questions.question: 'We read' is correctly
questions.explanation: उत्तम पुरुष बहुवचन = पठामः.

questions.question: In a formal letter, the subject line is introduced by the word
questions.explanation: विषयः names what the letter is about.

questions.question: A request/application letter in Sanskrit is called
questions.explanation: प्रार्थनापत्रम् = an application/request letter.

questions.question: The respectful salutation 'Respected Sir' in a formal letter is
questions.explanation: महोदय / मान्यवर is the formal salutation.

questions.question: A formal letter to the principal begins with
questions.explanation: सेवायाम् ('To…') opens a formal letter.

questions.question: The closing 'yours faithfully' for a MALE writer is
questions.explanation: भवदीयः (masculine) closes a formal letter.

questions.question: The formal closing used by a FEMALE writer is
questions.explanation: भवदीया is the feminine closing.

questions.question: An informal letter to a friend usually opens with
questions.explanation: प्रिय सखे / प्रियमित्र opens an informal letter.

questions.question: 'दिनाङ्कः' in a letter denotes the
questions.explanation: दिनाङ्कः = the date.

questions.question: 'प्रेषकः' in a letter refers to the
questions.explanation: प्रेषकः = the sender (one who sends).

questions.question: A suitable closing for an informal letter to a friend is
questions.explanation: भवतः मित्रम् / तव सुहृद् closes a friendly letter.

questions.question: In a leave application to the principal, the correct salutation is
questions.explanation: A formal letter uses महोदय / मान्यवर.

questions.question: A good विषयः line for a leave application is
questions.explanation: विषयः states the purpose: leave application.

questions.question: Which element does NOT belong in a formal letter?
questions.explanation: Formal letters avoid casual/slang language.

questions.question: The correct order of a formal letter is
questions.explanation: The skeleton runs address, subject, salutation, body, closing.

questions.question: 'सधन्यवादम्' at the end of a letter means
questions.explanation: सधन्यवादम् = 'with thanks'.

questions.question: A suitable warm greeting in a letter to your mother is
questions.explanation: An informal, respectful family greeting.

questions.question: A well-written अनुच्छेद (paragraph) has a beginning, a middle and
questions.explanation: आरम्भः, विस्तारः, उपसंहारः — beginning, middle, end.

questions.question: The first sentence of a paragraph is usually the
questions.explanation: The opening sentence names the topic (आरम्भः).

questions.question: A paragraph on 'मम विद्यालयः' would mainly describe
questions.explanation: विद्यालयः = school; the paragraph describes it.

questions.question: A short अनुच्छेद typically contains about
questions.explanation: A short paragraph is roughly 5–8 connected sentences.

questions.question: 'निबन्धः' means
questions.explanation: निबन्धः = essay (a longer, multi-paragraph composition).

questions.question: A suitable opening sentence for an essay on वृक्षाः is
questions.explanation: It names the topic (trees) at the start.

questions.question: The concluding sentence of a paragraph should
options: summarise or round off the idea
questions.answer: summarise or round off the idea
questions.explanation: उपसंहारः concludes the paragraph.

questions.question: Paragraph writing mainly builds the skill of
options: writing connected sentences on one topic
questions.answer: writing connected sentences on one topic
questions.explanation: An अनुच्छेद keeps to one topic with linked sentences.

questions.question: Hindi 'मैं विद्यालय जाता हूँ' in Sanskrit is
questions.explanation: अहम् + विद्यालयम् (object) + गच्छामि.

questions.question: Hindi 'सूरज उगता है' in Sanskrit is
questions.explanation: सूर्यः (subject) + उदयति (rises).

questions.question: English 'The sun rises' in Sanskrit is
questions.explanation: उदयति = rises.

questions.question: Hindi 'वह पुस्तक पढ़ती है' in Sanskrit is
questions.explanation: सा (she) + पुस्तकम् (object) + पठति.

questions.question: English 'We are students' in Sanskrit is
questions.explanation: वयम् + छात्राः + स्मः (we are).

questions.question: 'रामः फलम् खादति' means
questions.explanation: खादति = eats.

questions.question: 'जलं शीतलम् अस्ति' means
questions.explanation: शीतलम् = cold.

questions.question: Hindi 'तुम कहाँ जाते हो?' in Sanskrit is
questions.explanation: त्वम् (you) + कुत्र (where) + गच्छसि.

questions.question: 'बालकाः क्रीडन्ति' means
questions.explanation: बालकाः (plural) + क्रीडन्ति (play).

questions.question: English 'I have a book' is best rendered as
questions.explanation: Sanskrit uses षष्ठी + अस्ति for 'have': मम पुस्तकम् अस्ति.

questions.question: 'गुरुः शिष्यं पाठयति' means
questions.explanation: गुरुः (teacher) + शिष्यम् (student, object) + पाठयति (teaches).

questions.question: 'नदी वहति' means
questions.explanation: वहति = flows.

questions.question: चित्रवर्णनम् means
questions.explanation: चित्र (picture) + वर्णनम् (description).

questions.question: Picture description is usually written in which tense?
questions.explanation: चित्रवर्णन uses the present tense.

questions.question: To say 'in the picture there is a river' we write
questions.explanation: चित्रे (locative) … अस्ति frame.

questions.question: 'चित्रे' is which विभक्ति of चित्र?
questions.explanation: चित्रे = 'in the picture' (अधिकरण, सप्तमी).

questions.question: A good picture description includes
options: objects, actions and colours in the scene
questions.answer: objects, actions and colours in the scene
questions.explanation: Name वस्तूनि, क्रियाः and वर्णाः.

questions.question: 'आकाशे खगाः उड्डयन्ते' describes
questions.explanation: आकाशे (in the sky) खगाः (birds) उड्डयन्ते (fly).

questions.question: 'Children are playing in the picture' is
questions.explanation: चित्रे (locative) + बालकाः + क्रीडन्ति.

questions.question: At school level a picture description is usually about
questions.explanation: Roughly five simple present-tense sentences.

questions.question: In 'रामः वनं गच्छति', 'वनम्' is which कारक?
questions.explanation: वनम् is the object of motion (द्वितीया).

questions.question: The करण कारक (instrument, 'by/with') takes which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: करण = तृतीया विभक्ति (हस्तेन, लेखन्या).

questions.question: In 'वृक्षात् पत्रं पतति', 'वृक्षात्' is which कारक/case?
questions.explanation: Source 'from the tree' = अपादान, पञ्चमी.

questions.question: 'रामस्य पुस्तकम्' shows which relation/case?
questions.explanation: 'Rama's' = possession = षष्ठी.

questions.question: In 'सः ग्रामे वसति', 'ग्रामे' is
questions.explanation: Location 'in the village' = अधिकरण, सप्तमी.

questions.question: The सम्प्रदान कारक ('to/for whom') takes which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: सम्प्रदान = चतुर्थी (गुरवे नमः).

questions.question: सन्धि: देव + आलयः =
questions.explanation: अ + आ = आ (दीर्घ-सन्धि).

questions.question: सन्धि: सूर्य + उदयः =
questions.explanation: अ + उ = ओ (गुण-सन्धि).

questions.question: समास: 'रामलक्ष्मणौ' is a
questions.explanation: राम च लक्ष्मणः च = द्वन्द्व.

questions.question: समास: 'राजपुत्रः' is a
questions.explanation: राज्ञः पुत्रः = षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेद: नास्ति =
questions.explanation: अ + अ = आ; split back to न + अस्ति.

questions.question: In Sanskrit the कर्ता (subject) is in प्रथमा विभक्ति.
questions.explanation: The doer is always in प्रथमा (nominative).

questions.question: 'बालकाः पठति' is grammatically correct.
questions.explanation: A plural subject बालकाः needs the plural verb पठन्ति.

questions.question: A formal letter to the principal begins with 'प्रियमित्र'.
questions.explanation: A formal letter begins with सेवायाम्; प्रियमित्र is informal.

questions.question: 'भवदीयः' is used by a MALE writer to close a formal letter.
questions.explanation: भवदीयः (masc.) / भवदीया (fem.) close formal letters.

questions.question: A good अनुच्छेद should stick to one main topic.
questions.explanation: A paragraph keeps to a single topic with connected sentences.

questions.question: 'अहं गच्छामि' means 'I go'.
questions.explanation: अहम् = I; गच्छामि = (I) go.

questions.question: चित्रवर्णन is normally written in the past tense.
questions.explanation: Picture description is written in the present tense (लट्).

questions.question: In 'हस्तेन लिखति', हस्तेन is तृतीया (करण कारक).
questions.explanation: Instrument 'by the hand' takes तृतीया.

questions.question: The सन्धि विद्या + आलयः gives विद्यालयः.
questions.explanation: आ + आ = आ produces विद्यालयः.

questions.question: 'सा पठति' refers to a male ('he').
questions.explanation: सा = 'she'; 'he' would be सः.

questions.question: The कर्ता (doer) of a sentence takes ____ विभक्ति (case).
questions.explanation: The subject is in प्रथमा (nominative).

questions.question: Complete: 'The boy reads' — बालकः ____।
questions.explanation: प्रथम पुरुष एकवचन of पठ् = पठति.

questions.question: The plural (nominative) of बालकः is ____.
questions.explanation: बहुवचन प्रथमा of बालक = बालकाः.

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for 'I' is ____.
questions.explanation: अहम् = I (उत्तम पुरुष).

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for 'you' (singular) is ____.
questions.explanation: त्वम् = you (मध्यम पुरुष एकवचन).

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for 'she' is ____.
questions.explanation: सा = she; सः = he.

questions.question: In a formal letter the subject line is introduced by ____.
questions.explanation: विषयः names the letter's purpose.

questions.question: A request/application letter is called ____.
questions.explanation: प्रार्थनापत्रम् = application letter.

questions.question: 'in the picture' in Sanskrit is ____.
questions.explanation: चित्रे is सप्तमी (locative) of चित्र.

questions.question: The करण कारक (instrument) takes ____ विभक्ति.
questions.explanation: करण = तृतीया विभक्ति.

questions.question: सन्धि: सत् + जनः = ____.
questions.explanation: व्यञ्जन-सन्धि: त् + ज = ज्ज.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेद: नास्ति = न + ____.
questions.explanation: नास्ति splits into न + अस्ति.

questions.question: An essay in Sanskrit is called ____.
questions.explanation: निबन्धः = essay.

questions.question: 'they read' (बहुवचन) is ____.
questions.explanation: प्रथम पुरुष बहुवचन of पठ् = पठन्ति.

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for 'water' is ____.
questions.explanation: जलम् = water (नपुंसकलिङ्ग).

questions.question: Write one simple Sanskrit sentence and label its कर्ता, कर्म and क्रिया.
questions.answer: Example: बालकः फलं खादति। कर्ता = बालकः (प्रथमा, the doer); कर्म = फलम् (द्वितीया, the object); क्रिया = खादति (the verb 'eats').
questions.explanation: A basic sentence = subject (प्रथमा) + object (द्वितीया) + agreeing verb.

questions.question: Give the present-tense (लट्) forms of the root पठ् for अहम्, त्वम् and सः.
questions.answer: अहम् → पठामि; त्वम् → पठसि; सः → पठति. (I read / you read / he reads.)
questions.explanation: Verb changes by पुरुष: उत्तम पठामि, मध्यम पठसि, प्रथम पठति.

questions.question: Change to the plural: बालकः फलं खादति।
questions.answer: बालकाः फलानि खादन्ति। (The boys eat fruits.)
questions.explanation: Subject, object and verb all become plural.

questions.question: Form the Sanskrit sentence for 'The girls sing.'
questions.explanation: बहुवचन subject बालिकाः + बहुवचन verb गायन्ति.

questions.question: List the main parts of a formal Sanskrit letter (any five).
questions.answer: सेवायाम् (address), दिनाङ्कः (date), विषयः (subject line), महोदय (salutation), body (विषय-वस्तु), and closing भवदीयः/भवदीया with the sender's name.
questions.explanation: These are the fixed elements of an औपचारिक पत्र.

questions.question: What salutation and closing do you use in a letter to the principal?
questions.answer: Salutation: महोदय (or मान्यवर). Closing: भवदीयः (male) / भवदीया (female), with the student's name and class.
questions.explanation: Formal letters use महोदय and भवदीयः/भवदीया.

questions.question: Write a suitable विषयः (subject line) for a two-day leave application.
questions.answer: विषयः — द्विदिनावकाशार्थं प्रार्थनापत्रम्। (Subject: application for two days' leave.)
questions.explanation: The विषयः states the purpose in one line.

questions.question: State two ways an informal letter to a friend differs from a formal one.
questions.answer: (1) Salutation/closing are warm (प्रिय सखे / भवतः मित्रम्) instead of महोदय / भवदीयः. (2) It omits सेवायाम् and विषयः and uses friendly, personal language.
questions.explanation: Informal letters are personal; formal letters follow a fixed official skeleton.

questions.question: What are the three parts of a good अनुच्छेद?
questions.answer: आरम्भः (opening/topic sentence), विस्तारः (middle with details), and उपसंहारः (concluding sentence).
questions.explanation: Beginning, middle and end on one topic.

questions.question: Write two opening sentences for a paragraph on 'मम विद्यालयः'.
questions.answer: मम विद्यालयः अतीव सुन्दरः अस्ति। सः नगरस्य मध्ये स्थितः अस्ति। (My school is very beautiful. It is in the middle of the town.)
questions.explanation: The first sentences name the topic (the school) and add a detail.

questions.question: Translate to Sanskrit: 'I drink water.' and 'She reads a book.'
questions.answer: अहं जलं पिबामि। सा पुस्तकं पठति।
questions.explanation: Fix कर्ता (अहम्/सा), कर्म (जलम्/पुस्तकम्, द्वितीया) and agreeing verb.

questions.question: Translate to English: 'वयं छात्राः स्मः। गुरुः पाठयति।'
questions.answer: We are students. The teacher teaches.
questions.explanation: वयम् = we, स्मः = are; गुरुः पाठयति = the teacher teaches.

questions.question: Translate the Hindi sentence 'सूरज उगता है' into Sanskrit.
questions.explanation: सूर्यः (subject) + उदयति (rises).

questions.question: Write three Sanskrit sentences (present tense) describing a picture of a garden.
questions.answer: चित्रे एकम् उद्यानम् अस्ति। उद्याने बहवः वृक्षाः सन्ति। बालकाः तत्र क्रीडन्ति।
questions.explanation: Uses the चित्रे … अस्ति/सन्ति frame in the present tense.

questions.question: Why is चित्रवर्णन written in the present tense, and what is the case of 'चित्रे'?
questions.answer: Because it describes what is happening in the scene right now, so the present tense (लट्) is used. 'चित्रे' is सप्तमी विभक्ति (locative, 'in the picture').
questions.explanation: Present tense suits an ongoing scene; चित्रे = अधिकरण/सप्तमी.

questions.question: Name the six कारक and give one विभक्ति for each.
questions.answer: कर्ता–प्रथमा, कर्म–द्वितीया, करण–तृतीया, सम्प्रदान–चतुर्थी, अपादान–पञ्चमी, अधिकरण–सप्तमी (सम्बन्ध–षष्ठी is a relation, not strictly a कारक).
questions.explanation: Each role maps to a case ending.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि: देव + आलयः and सूर्य + उदयः.
questions.answer: देव + आलयः = देवालयः (अ+आ=आ); सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः (अ+उ=ओ).
questions.explanation: दीर्घ-सन्धि and गुण-सन्धि.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split): सज्जनः and विद्यालयः.
questions.answer: सज्जनः = सत् + जनः; विद्यालयः = विद्या + आलयः.
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form into its parts.

questions.question: Identify the समास: रामलक्ष्मणौ and राजपुत्रः.
questions.answer: रामलक्ष्मणौ = द्वन्द्व-समासः (राम च लक्ष्मणः च); राजपुत्रः = तत्पुरुष-समासः (राज्ञः पुत्रः).
questions.explanation: द्वन्द्व joins equals; तत्पुरुष has a case-relation.

questions.question: Make the sentence negative: सः पठति।
questions.answer: सः न पठति। (He does not read.)
questions.explanation: Place न before the verb to negate.

questions.question: Define निबन्धः and अनुच्छेदः in one line each.
questions.answer: अनुच्छेदः = a short group of connected sentences on one topic (a paragraph). निबन्धः = a longer, multi-paragraph composition (an essay).
questions.explanation: Paragraph vs essay.

questions.question: Write a suitable opening and closing line for an informal letter to a friend.
questions.answer: Opening: प्रिय सखे मोहन, सप्रेम नमः। Closing: भवतः मित्रम्, सुरेशः।
questions.explanation: Warm greeting and friendly sign-off.

questions.question: Write a short formal प्रार्थनापत्र (application) in Sanskrit to your principal requesting two days' leave. Keep the proper structure.
questions.answer:
सेवायाम्,
श्रीमान् प्रधानाचार्यः,
शासकीय-उच्च-विद्यालयः, अमुकनगरम्।
दिनाङ्कः — १० जुलै, २०२६
विषयः — द्विदिनावकाशार्थं प्रार्थनापत्रम्।
महोदय,
सविनयं निवेदनम् अस्ति यत् अहं ज्वरेण पीडितः अस्मि, अतः विद्यालयम् आगन्तुं न शक्नोमि। कृपया मह्यं द्वयोः दिनयोः अवकाशं दातुम् अर्हन्ति। अहं भवतां कृते कृतज्ञः भविष्यामि।
सधन्यवादम्।
भवदीयः शिष्यः,
रमेशः, दशमी कक्षा।
questions.explanation: The letter shows all formal parts: सेवायाम्, दिनाङ्कः, विषयः, महोदय, body, and भवदीयः with name/class.

questions.question: Write a short informal letter (5–6 lines) in Sanskrit to a friend inviting him to your birthday.
questions.answer:
प्रिय सखे मोहन,
सप्रेम नमः। अहं कुशली अस्मि, आशासे त्वम् अपि कुशली असि। आगामिनि रविवासरे मम जन्मदिवसः अस्ति। मम गृहे लघु-उत्सवः भविष्यति। त्वं सायं पञ्चवादने अवश्यम् आगच्छ। तव आगमनेन अहं प्रसन्नः भविष्यामि।
भवतः मित्रम्,
सुरेशः।
questions.explanation: An informal letter uses प्रिय सखे / सप्रेम नमः and closes with भवतः मित्रम्; it is warm and personal.

questions.question: Write a short अनुच्छेद (5–6 sentences) in Sanskrit on 'मम प्रियः ऋतुः' (my favourite season) with an English meaning.
questions.answer:
मम प्रियः ऋतुः वसन्तः अस्ति। वसन्ते वृक्षेषु नवीनानि पत्राणि पुष्पाणि च भवन्ति। सर्वत्र हरितं शोभनं च दृश्यते। खगाः मधुरं गायन्ति। जनाः प्रसन्नाः भवन्ति। अतः वसन्तः मह्यं रोचते।
(My favourite season is spring. In spring, new leaves and flowers appear on the trees. Everywhere it looks green and lovely. Birds sing sweetly. People become happy. Therefore spring pleases me.)
questions.explanation: The paragraph names the topic, gives details, and ends with a concluding feeling (आरम्भः–विस्तारः–उपसंहारः).

questions.question: Translate this short passage into Sanskrit and note the verbs you used: 'I am a student. I read Sanskrit every day. My teacher teaches well. We love Sanskrit.'
questions.answer: अहं छात्रः अस्मि। अहं प्रतिदिनं संस्कृतं पठामि। मम गुरुः सम्यक् पाठयति। वयं संस्कृतं स्निह्यामः। — Verbs used: अस्मि (am), पठामि (read), पाठयति (teaches), स्निह्यामः (love).
questions.explanation: Each sentence keeps कर्ता, कर्म (द्वितीया) and an agreeing verb; note person/number changes.

questions.question: Describe a village scene picture in five Sanskrit sentences (present tense) and give the English meaning.
questions.answer:
चित्रे एकः ग्रामः अस्ति। ग्रामे लघूनि गृहाणि सन्ति। एका नदी वहति। कृषकाः क्षेत्रे कार्यं कुर्वन्ति। बालकाः वृक्षस्य अधः क्रीडन्ति।
(In the picture there is a village. In the village there are small houses. A river flows. Farmers work in the field. Children play under a tree.)
questions.explanation: Five present-tense sentences naming objects and actions with the चित्रे … अस्ति/सन्ति frame.

questions.question: Explain how कर्तृ-क्रिया (subject–verb) agreement works in Sanskrit, with singular, dual and plural examples.
questions.answer: The verb must agree with the subject in number (वचन) and person (पुरुष). Using पठ्: एकवचन बालकः पठति (one boy reads); द्विवचन बालकौ पठतः (two boys read); बहुवचन बालकाः पठन्ति (many boys read). The subject-ending and the verb-ending change together; a plural subject with a singular verb (बालकाः पठति) is wrong.
questions.explanation: Agreement is the core rule of वाक्यरचना: number and person of subject and verb must match.

questions.question: Explain the six कारक with one Sanskrit example sentence for each.
questions.answer: कर्ता–प्रथमा: रामः गच्छति (Rama goes). कर्म–द्वितीया: रामः फलं खादति (Rama eats a fruit). करण–तृतीया: सः हस्तेन लिखति (he writes with the hand). सम्प्रदान–चतुर्थी: सः गुरवे नमति (he bows to the teacher). अपादान–पञ्चमी: वृक्षात् पत्रं पतति (a leaf falls from the tree). अधिकरण–सप्तमी: सः ग्रामे वसति (he lives in the village).
questions.explanation: Each कारक (role) is shown by its विभक्ति (ending) with a model sentence.

questions.question: Explain three types of सन्धि and two समास with examples used in composition.
questions.answer: सन्धि: (1) दीर्घ-सन्धि — देव + आलयः = देवालयः (अ+आ=आ). (2) गुण-सन्धि — सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः (अ+उ=ओ). (3) व्यञ्जन-सन्धि — सत् + जनः = सज्जनः. समास: (1) द्वन्द्व — रामलक्ष्मणौ (राम च लक्ष्मणः च). (2) तत्पुरुष — राजपुत्रः (राज्ञः पुत्रः).
questions.explanation: सन्धि merges sounds; समास compacts words — both make writing tighter.

questions.question:
Read this partial formal letter and answer:
'________ ,
श्रीमान् प्रधानाचार्यः, ... विद्यालयः।
विषयः — अवकाशार्थं प्रार्थनापत्रम्।
महोदय, ... भवदीयः, रमेशः।'
Which word should fill the blank at the very top, and which two parts show it is a FORMAL letter?
questions.answer: The blank should be 'सेवायाम्'. It is formal because it uses सेवायाम् with the addressee and the salutation महोदय (and closing भवदीयः) — none of which appear in an informal letter.
questions.explanation: सेवायाम्, महोदय and भवदीयः are hallmarks of an औपचारिक (formal) letter.

questions.question: A student must translate these Hindi sentences into Sanskrit: (1) 'मैं जल पीता हूँ।' (2) 'वह विद्यालय जाता है।' Write both Sanskrit sentences.
questions.answer: (1) अहं जलं पिबामि। (2) सः विद्यालयं गच्छति।
questions.explanation: Fix कर्ता (अहम्/सः), कर्म in द्वितीया (जलम्/विद्यालयम्) and an agreeing verb.

questions.question: A paragraph reads: 'मम विद्यालयः सुन्दरः अस्ति। अत्र बहवः अध्यापकाः सन्ति। पुस्तकालयः अपि अस्ति। ____' The concluding sentence is missing. Supply a suitable उपसंहारः in Sanskrit and say why it fits.
questions.answer: A suitable conclusion: 'अहं मम विद्यालयं बहु स्निह्यामि।' (I love my school very much.) It fits because a paragraph should end with a concluding sentence (उपसंहारः) that rounds off the topic with the writer's feeling.
questions.explanation: The last sentence must conclude the single topic (the school).

questions.question: You are shown a picture of the sky with birds and a rising sun. Write three Sanskrit sentences (present tense) describing it.
questions.answer: चित्रे आकाशः अस्ति। आकाशे खगाः उड्डयन्ते। सूर्यः उदयति।
questions.explanation: Present-tense sentences using the चित्रे … अस्ति frame; names objects and actions.

questions.question: Read the sentence: 'रामः ग्रामे हस्तेन पत्रं लिखति।' Identify the कारक/विभक्ति of ग्रामे, हस्तेन and पत्रम्.
questions.answer: ग्रामे = अधिकरण, सप्तमी ('in the village'). हस्तेन = करण, तृतीया ('with the hand'). पत्रम् = कर्म, द्वितीया (the object 'a letter').
questions.explanation: Each noun's role is shown by its विभक्ति ending.

questions.question: Given the words बालकः / पुस्तकम् / पठति, arrange them into a correct Sanskrit sentence and label the कर्ता, कर्म and क्रिया.
questions.answer: Sentence: बालकः पुस्तकं पठति। कर्ता = बालकः (प्रथमा), कर्म = पुस्तकम् (द्वितीया), क्रिया = पठति.
questions.explanation: Natural order कर्ता–कर्म–क्रिया with correct endings.

questions.question: A student named Sita (a girl) needs one day's leave. Write a suitable विषयः line and the salutation and closing she should use in her application.
questions.answer: विषयः — एकदिनावकाशार्थं प्रार्थनापत्रम्। Salutation: महोदय। Closing: भवदीया, सीता (feminine भवदीया because the writer is a girl).
questions.explanation: Formal salutation महोदय; a female writer signs off with भवदीया.

questions.question: Translate these English sentences into Sanskrit: (1) 'The boys play.' (2) 'We are students.'
questions.explanation: Plural subjects take plural verbs (क्रीडन्ति, स्मः).

questions.question: The sentence 'छात्राः पठति।' has an agreement error. Identify the error and write the corrected sentence.
questions.answer: Error: the subject छात्राः is plural (बहुवचन) but the verb पठति is singular. Corrected: छात्राः पठन्ति। (The students read.)
questions.explanation: Subject and verb must agree in number; plural subject needs पठन्ति.

questions.question: Join these word-pairs using सन्धि: (1) देव + आलयः (2) सूर्य + उदयः (3) न + अस्ति.
questions.explanation: Applying दीर्घ and गुण सन्धि in composition.
